assertions.text: Precision after verification is at least 0.8
assertions.how: a grader who has not seen the run maps each confirmed finding that is not a deterministic tool finding to one seeded defect, to 'real but not seeded' (with the reason it is a genuine problem for these users), or to 'not a problem'; precision = (seeded + real but not seeded) / confirmed judged findings >= 0.8. Also report the strict precision, seeded / confirmed judged findings, and the recall by meaning

assertions.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
assertions.how: the final reply lists the confirmed problems from most to least severe, or the P0/P1 first, and names what the agent could not check (needs-human WCAG items, real skippers)

findings.title: Touch-primary controls closer than 8 px: "Saturday 17 October, open" and "Reserve this tool"
findings.description: On the 768 px touch viewport, the hit areas of these primary controls are 0 px apart (edge to edge); they need ≥ 8 px.

findings.title: Clipped text in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: Text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") overflows a box with overflow hidden at 320 px (scroll 327×46 vs client 184×46, axis x).

findings.title: Focus order jumps back: "Electric wet tile saw, 180 mm" → "Search tools"
findings.description: After "Electric wet tile saw, 180 mm", Tab moves to "Search tools", which sits 654 px above it in the same column; the focus order does not follow the visual reading order (clear-inversion heuristic).

findings.title: Basket pick-up sessions are shown in reverse order to their reading and focus order
findings.description: Sessions should be presented, read and focused in the same order, ideally by date. In the DOM and ARIA snapshot the six radios run Saturday 10 October to Wednesday 28 October. On screen they are reversed: at 320 px Wednesday 28 October is at the top and Saturday 10 October at the bottom; at 1280 px Wednesday 28 October fills a full-width first row and the rest run right to left, Saturday 24 to Saturday 10. Probe 72: Tab into the group lands on Saturday 10 October, which is at the bottom right, and ArrowDown moves to and selects Wednesday 14 October, the card to its left.

findings.title: Esc does not close the loan-length listbox
findings.description: With #loan-list open, pressing Esc leaves it open and does not return focus to #loan-button.

findings.title: Tab and Shift+Tab cannot leave the open loan-length listbox
findings.description: Focus cycles among the options until one is chosen; this duplicates F-0034.

findings.title: Session-day dots disappear under forced colours at 320 px, leaving open days unmarked
findings.description: Under forced colours, meaningful indicators should stay visible. At 320 px the calendar marks session days only with a small dot (the 'Open' text appears only at wider widths). In the 320 px forced-colours captures the dots are gone, so days 10, 14, 17, 21, 24 and 28 look identical to closed days. The accessible names still say 'open'.

findings.title: Tool card and basket item headings share the level of the section heading that contains them
findings.description: Headings should nest as they do visually. On the find page each tool card name is an h2 inside the 'Tools' region whose own heading is h2; on the basket page the item heading 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' is h2 inside the 'Tools' h2 section. Visually the card names are subordinate to 'Tools'.

findings.title: Basket asks for a pick-up session without preselecting the day already chosen on the tool page
findings.description: Members should not have to remember and re-make a choice the flow already has. On the tool page the member chose Saturday 17 October; the basket line repeats 'Pick up Saturday 17 October', but none of the six session radios is selected, the Saturday 17 October option sits in the middle of a reversed list, and Continue without a choice shows an error.

findings.title: Results grid column minimum of 330 px is wider than a 320 px viewport
findings.description: Content should reflow to a single column without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10). .results uses grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(330px, 1fr)); at 320 px the page has 288 px of content width after its 16 px side padding, so the single column is forced to 330 px and the cards overflow the viewport by about 42 px.

findings.title: Search with no matches leaves the previous results and status unchanged
findings.description: A search that matches nothing should replace the list with an empty state and announce it (CMP-05). search() only renders and updates #results-status when list.length is non-zero; with zero matches it does nothing, so the old cards stay on screen and the live region keeps its old count. The page has no empty-state markup at all.

findings.title: Tab key is captured inside the loan-length list, so keyboard focus cannot leave it
findings.description: Keyboard users must be able to move focus away from any component (WCAG 2.1.2). The listbox keydown handler treats Tab like ArrowDown and calls preventDefault, cycling focus among the options; Shift+Tab is caught too because the check is e.key === 'Tab'. Focus only leaves when an option is activated with Enter or Space.

findings.title: Each press of Confirm reservation creates another reservation while the request is pending
findings.description: A submit that creates a record should be guarded against repeat activation. The confirm submit handler allocates a reference (FT-4471 + count) and pushes it into sessionStorage 'reservations' before its 1.5 s wait, and the button is neither disabled nor guarded; a second press during the wait allocates a second reference. The done page then lists both ('FT-4471 and FT-4472', label 'Reservation numbers').

findings.title: Continue and Confirm reservation show no visible pending state during their 1.2 s and 1.5 s waits
findings.description: An action that takes longer than about 1 s should show it is in progress (CMP-04). Both handlers only set aria-busy='true' on the button; styles.css has no [aria-busy] rule, the label does not change and nothing else on the page changes until navigation or the error.

findings.title: Expired basket hold is reported only as 'Something went wrong. Try again.'
findings.description: An error message should state what happened and what to do (H9). When the 10-minute hold has passed, Continue shows the generic 'Something went wrong. Try again.' in the error summary. The page never mentions a time limit beyond 'Items are held for you while you finish', and there is no visible countdown.

findings.title: Once the hold has expired, Continue fails on every retry
findings.description: A recoverable error should be recoverable from the page that shows it. hold_started is set once and only cleared by the 'Reserve another tool' link on the done page; startHoldIfNeeded() never restarts an expired hold, removing items or re-adding tools does not reset it, and holdExpired() stays true. Every later Continue in the same tab shows the same error, although the message says 'Try again.'

findings.title: Calendar lets closed days and days before the tool's availability date be chosen and added without warning
findings.description: Every day button can be chosen and Reserve adds it; this overlaps F-0062.

findings.title: Confirm accepts a pick-up day before the tool's 'Available from' date
findings.description: A pressure washer picked for Sat 10 Oct (available from 17 Oct) reaches 'Reservation confirmed' with no error.

findings.title: Closed-day error on confirm comes late and has no link to change the day
findings.description: The day is rejected only after Confirm, and the error item offers no route back to the calendar.

findings.title: Per-tool pick-up day and the basket's pick-up session are separate choices that are never reconciled
findings.description: One flow should collect one pick-up time. The tool page stores a pick-up day per item; the basket then asks for a pick-up session for the whole basket from all six sessions. Nothing checks that the session matches the items' days, so the confirm summary can show 'pick up Saturday 17 October' for a tool and 'Saturday 10 October' as the session, and the reservation goes through.

findings.title: Dark-theme success colour drifts from the declared token and the available badge background matches the card
findings.description: Dark mode should use design.md's success #8fd1a8 on selection #24352c. styles.css sets --color-ok: #2f7d4a and --color-ok-tint: #1d2622, which equals the dark --color-surface. 'Available from' text in .badge--ok (16 px bold, not large text) computes to about 3.1:1 on #1d2622, below 4.5:1, and the badge has no visible fill on the card.

findings.title: Find page shows the search form above the results but its DOM and tab order put results first
findings.description: Focus order should follow the visual order (WCAG 2.4.3, 1.3.2). In the DOM .finder__results precedes .finder__form; above 480 px CSS order puts the form first visually. Keyboard users therefore tab through all ten card links before reaching the search field shown above them. At 480 px and below the visual order matches the DOM, with the search form below all results.

findings.title: Fixed action bar on the tool page covers the end of the page
findings.description: Fixed bars should not hide content or focused controls (WCAG 2.4.11). .actionbar is position: fixed with min-height 72 px, but .page--bar reduces the main bottom padding to 8 px and nothing reserves space for the bar, so the last calendar row and the footer can sit under it at the end of the scroll; a calendar day reached by Tab near the bottom of the viewport can be hidden behind the bar.

findings.title: 'Choose a pick-up day first.' is not announced when Reserve is pressed without a day
findings.description: An error should be programmatically tied to the control and announced (WCAG 3.3.1, 4.1.3). #day-error is a plain paragraph that is unhidden with no live region and no aria-describedby from the calendar group or day buttons; focus moves to the first day button, so a screen reader announces that day ('Friday 9 October') and not the error.

findings.title: Tool names are cut to one line, so near-identical names become indistinguishable
findings.description: Long labels should wrap rather than truncate where the ending distinguishes items. .card__name a uses white-space: nowrap with text-overflow: ellipsis and no title or other full-name cue. 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and '... one battery' differ only at the end, which is the part removed on narrow cards.

findings.title: Tool names in result cards and basket rows are h2 elements nested under an h2 'Tools' heading
findings.description: Heading levels should reflect structure (WCAG 1.3.1). Find-page cards render <h2 class="card__name"> inside the section headed by h2 'Tools'; basket rows render <h2 class="h3"> under h2 'Tools', and the .h3 class is not defined in styles.css, so those names take the full 22 px h2 size and margin.

findings.title: Membership and mobile number checks reject common formats without normalising them
findings.description: Inputs should accept reasonable variants and normalise them (H5, CPY). The membership check /^FT-\d{5}$/ rejects lower-case 'ft-01234' and a missing hyphen; the mobile check /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/ rejects '+44 7700 900123', '07700-900123' and '07700 900 123'. Only the trim is applied. The phone hint does not show the expected format until the error appears.

findings.title: Confirmation page shows reservation number FT-4471 when no reservation exists
findings.description: A confirmation should only show a reference that was issued. initDone falls back to the literal 'FT-4471' when no stored reservation matches, so opening done.html directly, after the session ends, or with a mismatched slot shows 'Reservation confirmed' with a number that was never allocated.

findings.title: The three-tools limit stated on the find page is not enforced when adding to the basket
findings.description: A stated constraint should be enforced where it applies (H5). The intro says members can reserve up to three tools at a time, but the Reserve handler adds any number of tools to the basket and neither basket nor confirm checks the count.

findings.title: Unknown tool id silently shows the first tool's page
findings.description: A missing record should show a not-found state. initTool uses toolById(id) || TOOLS[0], so a stale or mistyped link opens the 18 V two-battery drill page, and Reserve adds that drill.

findings.title: Done page repeats the first tool's name in a hidden span after the tools list
findings.description: Hidden text should not duplicate visible content. #c-tool, an sr-only span inside the Tools definition, is filled with the first tool's name, so screen readers read the tools list and then the first tool again.

findings.title: 'Reserve this tool' only adds to a basket; nothing tells a first-time member the reservation is unfinished
findings.description: Journey reserve-tool-for-saturday, steps 6-7. The persona taps 'Reserve this tool' expecting the drill to be reserved. The only response is a toast 'Added to your basket' that overlays the calendar and is gone within 5 s, plus the header count changing to 'Basket (1)'. The button label is unchanged and the toast has no link onward. The persona has every reason to believe the job is done and close the page (CW-Q1 fails at step 7: the basket checkout is a hidden prerequisite). The feedback also names a different effect from the one the button promised (CW-Q4 fails at step 6). Missing knowledge: that 'Reserve' means 'hold in basket' and two more screens remain. Missing feedback: a lasting message that the reservation is not complete and a direct way to continue. Step verdicts: step 6 would_with_effort, step 7 would_not.

findings.title: Basket asks for a pick-up session again and does not carry over the pick-up day just chosen
findings.description: Journey reserve-tool-for-saturday, step 8. The persona chose Saturday 17 October on the tool page, and the basket card repeats 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'. Below it, 'Pick-up session' lists six sessions with none selected. To the persona this is the same question again; the likely action is to press Continue straight away and hit an error. Missing knowledge: that the day and the session are separate choices and the session is not set from the day. Step verdict would_with_effort.

findings.title: The two cordless drills are truncated to identical names in the tool list on phones
findings.description: Journey reserve-tool-for-saturday, step 4. At 375 px both result cards read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' with identical category, deposit, availability and icon. The words that distinguish them ('two batteries' / 'one battery') are cut off. The persona specifically wants the two-battery drill and cannot tell which card it is. Missing knowledge: which card is which. Step verdict would_with_effort (recoverable by opening one and going back).

findings.title: Header still shows 'Basket (1)' on the 'Reservation confirmed' page
findings.description: Journey reserve-tool-for-saturday, step 13. The confirmation page is otherwise clear (reference FT-4471, the drill, Saturday 17 October 10:00 to 13:00, £20 to bring, what happens next), but the header still reads 'Basket (1)'. A first-time member, already unsure what the basket means after step 6, may read this as the drill still sitting unreserved in the basket. Missing feedback: a basket state consistent with the completed reservation. Step verdict would_with_effort.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar accepts days on which the tool cannot be collected
findings.description: Only session days (marked Open / green dot) are library sessions, and each tool has an 'Available from' date. The calendar nevertheless lets any day be chosen and added: Monday 12 October (no session) was accepted for the drill and the basket then reads 'Pick up Monday 12 October'; for the pressure washer, available from Saturday 17 October, Saturday 10 October was accepted with 'Added to your basket'. No warning is shown at either point.

findings.title: Confirm summary shows two different collection dates after the session is changed
findings.description: After Change -> Wednesday 21 October -> Continue, the 'Your reservation' box reads Tools: '... one week, pick up Saturday 17 October' and Pick-up session: 'Wednesday 21 October, 18:00 to 20:00'. A summary should state one collection date.

findings.title: Change link opens the basket without the current session selected
findings.description: From confirm, 'Change' next to 'Saturday 17 October' goes to the basket where none of the six sessions is selected; the member must find and choose again even to keep the same one.

findings.title: Membership number typed on the confirm page is lost when leaving and returning
findings.description: Entered details should survive a detour. After typing FT-01234, using Change and returning, the Membership number field is empty. After confirming and pressing browser Back, the name and mobile are kept but the membership number is again empty.

findings.title: Filters button is an unlabelled icon
findings.description: The control that reveals 'Available from' and 'Category' shows only a three-line icon; its name 'Filters' exists only as an accessible name. Nothing visible says that a date filter is behind it.

findings.title: Basket says items are held but not for how long
findings.description: The basket states 'Items are held for you while you finish.' No hold time is given there, on the tool page after adding, or on the confirm page.

findings.title: Reservation number uses the same FT- prefix as membership numbers
findings.description: The done page gives 'Reservation number FT-4471' while membership numbers look like 'FT-01234'. The two identifiers share a format the member is told to bring.

findings.title: Removing a tool from the basket is immediate and cannot be undone
findings.description: Pressing Remove removes the tool at once; the basket count drops and there is no confirmation, message or undo. To get it back the member must find the tool again and re-enter the pick-up day and loan length.

findings.title: Green and grey availability badges differ only by colour, with no stated meaning
findings.description: Each card has an 'Available from …' badge. Most are green, but those for Sat 17, Wed 21 and Sat 24 October are grey; the page does not say what the difference means, and the text and accessible text are identical in form ('Available from Sat 17 Oct').

findings.title: Format errors on confirm are worded as if the field were empty
findings.description: When a value is entered in the wrong format, the message should say what is wrong. With '01234' in Membership number the error reads 'Enter your membership number, like FT-01234'; with '+44 7700 900123' in Mobile number it reads 'Enter a UK mobile number, like 07700 900123' — the same texts shown when the fields are blank.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph in place of a thumbnail
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical pale-green tile with a wrench, whether the tool is a ladder, pressure washer or wallpaper steamer. DESIGN.md lists 'a thumbnail' as part of the card, so this reads as a placeholder left on show.

findings.title: Brand identity is a stock wrench glyph and the name in body type
findings.description: The masthead and surfaces use a generic glyph, type and palette with nothing specific to the Fernhill library.

findings.title: Confirmation page has no focal point marking the completed reservation
findings.description: The done page presents the reservation as a plain definition card under the heading, with no visual emphasis on the reference or the moment of completion.

findings.title: Basket session cards break into one full-width row and five cramped cards at 1280
findings.description: Six session radios render as one full-width card (Wednesday 28 October) then five narrow cards whose labels wrap to three lines.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unthemed browser-default date and select controls
findings.description: 'Available from' is a native yyyy/mm/dd date input with the browser calendar icon, and Category is a native select with a different border and chevron from the styled Loan length select.

findings.title: Details list splits into two misaligned columns
findings.description: Category, Deposit and Available from align values at about x=224; Chuck, Batteries, Weight and Case align at about x=180, with a different row gap.

findings.title: No way for returning members to repeat a previous reservation
findings.description: Returning members say 'same as last time', but no route offers past reservations, a reorder or a 'recently borrowed' list. Each reservation starts from the full catalogue and asks for the membership number, name and mobile again.

findings.title: Tool names truncate to identical strings on phones
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut with an ellipsis; both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', and other titles lose the distinguishing spec ('Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Pressure washer, 130 ...').

findings.title: Basket and done pages end with an empty grey band under the footer
findings.description: At 1280 the footer stops mid-viewport and the page ground continues below it.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: On find, all ten cards use an identical wrench glyph in a pale-green square as the thumbnail. It carries no information, makes the two cordless drills and the two tile tools look the same, and is the largest visual element on each card.

findings.title: No identity floor: the product's only mark is the name in body text
findings.description: Across all five surfaces the identity is a small wrench glyph and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type. The membership-card green named in design.md as the source of the accent is not expressed beyond buttons and badges; nothing of the community centre, the desk or the volunteers appears visually.

findings.title: Drill names truncate to identical strings at 375
findings.description: Both cordless drill cards read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' at 375; duplicates F-0057.

findings.title: Search and filters sit below the full tool list at 375
findings.description: At 375 the search region follows all ten tool cards, out of the first viewport; duplicates F-0058.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions listed newest-first
findings.description: Sessions run from 28 October back to 10 October; this part duplicates F-0044/F-0056/F-0075.

findings.title: Session cards form an uneven row at 1280
findings.description: At 1280 the first session card spans the full width while the other five are squeezed into narrow cards whose text wraps to three lines.

findings.title: Tool details split into two misaligned label columns
findings.description: The Details block on the tool page has Category/Deposit/Available from with values at about x=224 and Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case with values at about x=180, so the two halves of one list do not align.

findings.title: Browser-default date and select controls in the filter panel
findings.description: Filters-open shows a native date input with 'yyyy/mm/dd' (not the en-GB format the brief requires) and a native select; the two field labels sit on different baselines.

findings.title: Empty grey band below the footer on short pages
findings.description: At 1280 on basket and done the footer ends mid-viewport with bare page ground beneath; duplicates F-0116.

findings.title: Confirm form and done next-steps card use only the left half of the content width
findings.description: At 1280 the confirm form fields and the done page 'What happens next' card stop at about x=707 while the summary card above spans the full 1088 px, leaving the right half empty.

findings.title: Masthead still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: On done, the nav reads 'Basket (1)', implying the confirmed tool is still held.

findings.title: No-results state shows the full tool list
findings.description: With 'sewing machine' in the search field, the captured no-results state shows all ten tools and no message, identical to the default state.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the chip background only on 'available' badges
findings.description: In dark mode the green 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges have no tinted background while the grey 'later' badges keep theirs, inverting the light theme's emphasis.

findings.title: On phones the search field sits below all ten tools
findings.description: At 375 the Search region comes after the full list; this duplicates F-0069.

findings.title: Tool names truncate to identical strings on phones
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut so both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...'; this duplicates F-0115.

findings.title: Main nav items wrap to two lines on phones
findings.description: At 375 'Find a tool', 'Basket (1)' and 'Opening times' each wrap onto two lines in the header.

findings.title: axe color-contrast: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
findings.description: Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds (serious impact). Fix any of the following: Element has insufficient color contrast of 3.07 (foreground color: #2f7d4a, background color: #1d2622, font size: 12.0pt (16px), font weight: bold). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1

findings.title: Text contrast below 4.5:1: "Available from Sat 10 Oct"
findings.description: Text "Available from Sat 10 Oct" (16 px, weight 700) has 3.07:1 against its computed background in the dark theme at 320 px; it needs 4.5:1.

findings.title: Text clips under the text-spacing override in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em and word spacing 0.16em, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px (scroll 427×50 vs client 390×50).

findings.title: Text clips at 200 % text size in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With the root font size at 200 %, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px.

findings.title: Overlapping text: #reserve
findings.description: At 1280 px, text of #reserve ("Reserve this tool") overlaps text of button.day:nth-of-type(9) > span.day__num ("17") by 16×14 px.

findings.title: Horizontal page overflow on /?items=ladder-3m
findings.description: scrollWidth 346 px > clientWidth 320 px at 320 px. Widest offender: #results > li:nth-of-type(1) extends 26 px past the viewport; 9 more.

findings.title: Content does not reflow at 320 px on /?items=ladder-3m
findings.description: scrollWidth 346 px > clientWidth 320 px at 320 px. Widest offender: #results > li:nth-of-type(1) extends 26 px past the viewport; 9 more.

findings.title: Body text closer than 16 px to the viewport edge: "Cleaning · deposit £30"
findings.description: Text starts 145 px from the left and ends 9.7 px from the right edge of a 320 px viewport; body text needs ≥ 16 px at widths below 768 px.

findings.title: Cramped padding: "Pressure washer, 130 bar Cleaning · depo"
findings.description: Inside this bordered or filled container (17 px text): horizontal inset 6.4 px < 8.5 px.

findings.title: Not reachable by keyboard: "Fernhill Tool Library"
findings.description: The a "Fernhill Tool Library" is tabbable in the DOM, but a complete Tab walk never reached it. People who use a keyboard or switch cannot operate it.

ground_truth.description: At 480 px and below the stylesheet reorders the page so the list of tools comes before the search form, and the only way to the 'Available from' date and the category filter is an icon-only button (three lines) that opens a collapsed panel below the list. A member who wants tools for a given Saturday sees ten cards first and no date control, so they are unlikely to notice that filtering by day exists. The document order is form then results, so keyboard focus also runs against the visual order.

A search with no matching tool (for example 'sewing machine') leaves the previous results on the page and shows no message: the status region stays empty and the list does not change. The member cannot tell whether the search ran, whether nothing matched, or whether the old list is the answer.

Tool names are kept on one line and cut with an ellipsis inside the card's text column. At phone widths 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery' both read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' (at 375 px; a character more or less at other widths), so a member cannot tell which card is the right one without opening each; only from about 480 px does the difference show. The full name is only in the link's hidden overflow.

In the dark theme the 'Available from' badge is a mid green (#2f7d4a) on the card surface (#1d2622), about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs; the light theme passes. Members who use dark mode on their phones get the availability line as the least legible text on the page.

The results grid asks for columns at least 330 px wide; at 320 px the content box is 288 px, so the cards run 42 px past it and the page scrolls sideways by 26 px. The same happens at 200% zoom on a 640 px window.

Every day in the calendar can be chosen, including the days the library is closed; only session days carry the word 'Open' (a green dot on a phone). Choosing a closed day highlights it and the page confirms 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October'. The reservation is refused three steps later, on the confirm page ('The library is closed on Monday 12 October…'), and the only way back to the calendar is the browser.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' shows 'Added to your basket' for 1.2 seconds and nothing else changes nearby; the only lasting sign is the basket count in the header, which on a phone is above the fold. A member who looked away, or who reads slowly, does not know whether the press worked and presses again.

The 'Reserve this tool' bar is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it: the page ends 8 px under the calendar and the footer runs under the bar. A day button that sits in the bottom 72 px of the window counts as visible to the browser, so Tab reaches it without scrolling and the bar covers the focused control: at 768 px wide (900 px tall) the first two rows of days, at 1280 px the third row; on a phone the footer and the desk phone number sit under the bar at the end of the page.

The loan-length list opens as a custom listbox. Inside it, Tab moves to the next option and wraps around, and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter.

The basket says 'Items are held for you while you finish' but shows no time; the hold is ten minutes from the first item and is kept only in the browser. When it has lapsed, Continue waits 1.2 seconds and then says 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which is not what happened and does not say what to do.

The pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse (row-reverse with reversed wrapping), so the earliest session appears last on screen, at the bottom of the stack on a phone and at the end of the row on a desktop, while coming first in the document. Tab moves from the rightmost card leftwards, against reading order, and a screen reader hears the sessions in an order a sighted member does not see.

'Confirm reservation' stays enabled while the request runs for 1.5 seconds, and nothing visible says that anything is happening. A second press, which is what people do when nothing seems to happen, allocates a second reservation number; the confirmation page then lists two reservations for one visit, and the desk holds the tool twice.

The 'Change' link beside the pick-up session returns to the basket without the chosen session, so a member who only wanted to look at the summary comes back to a basket with no session selected and has to choose again. Nothing says the choice was dropped.

The calendar neither marks nor disables the days before the tool's 'Available from' date, the basket offers every session, and confirm does not check: a wet tile saw available from Saturday 24 October reserved for Saturday 10 October ends on 'Reservation confirmed'. The member is told a tool will be waiting when it cannot be, and finds out at the desk.

Each tool keeps the pick-up day chosen on its tool page, the session is chosen separately in the basket, and nothing reconciles them: a drill to be picked up on Saturday 17 October can be confirmed for the Wednesday 21 session, the confirm page shows both dates and the done page only the session, so it is unclear which day the desk sets the tool aside for.

The loan-length button has no aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its accessible name is only its current value: a screen-reader user hears 'One week, button, collapsed' and is not told what is being chosen.

The membership number must match /^FT-\d{5}$/ and the mobile number /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/, with no normalising: 'ft-01234', 'Ft-01234' (what a phone's sentence capitalisation makes of it) and 'FT 01234' are rejected, and so are '07700 900 123' and '+44 7700 900123', the form phone autofill often supplies. Each gets an error whose example looks like what the member typed.

After 'Reservation confirmed' the basket is not emptied: the header still reads 'Basket (1)' and the basket still lists the tool as held, and going back to the confirm page and confirming again reserves the same tool a second time under a new number.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' with no day chosen shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.' in a paragraph with no role or live region that the calendar does not reference, so it is not announced, and focus moves to the first day button, a closed day before the tool is available. The message stays on screen after a day is chosen.

Below 480 px the word 'Open' on session days is hidden and an 8 px dot takes its place; what the dot means is only in the hint above the calendar. On the phone, the members' main device, which days the library opens is easy to miss. The seeder chose the dot to fit the calendar at phone widths; the second labeller and two reviews judged it a minor problem.

The find page says members may reserve up to three tools at a time, but the basket takes a fourth tool without a warning and the reservation is confirmed for four, so the desk has to turn the member away from some of them at collection.

With the membership number, name and mobile filled in, 'Change', the basket and Continue bring the member back to the confirm page with all three fields empty; the details are kept nowhere, so she types them again on a phone.

The tool page asked for a pick-up day and the basket line repeats it, yet no pick-up session is selected and Continue answers 'Choose a pick-up session', so the member enters the same date a second time, in another form, and can choose a different one.

On the done page the Tools entry holds the visible list item and a visually hidden span with the same name, so screen readers read the reserved tool's name twice; next to two reservation numbers this can sound like two tools.

The 'Available from' filter keeps the tools that can be collected on the chosen day, but its label uses the badges' words and its hint says 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day': choosing 14 October hides a tool available from 17 October, which could be picked up after the 14th.

'Reserve this tool' does not reserve: it puts the tool in a basket held for ten minutes, the button keeps its label, and nothing says that a basket, a session and a confirmation still follow. A first-time member can believe the tool is reserved and put the phone down, and the hold lapses with nothing reserved. It is the press D07 describes, read for a different harm: D07 is the brief feedback, this is the misleading action.

I reviewed the reservation flow from finding a tool to the confirmation page. It isn't ready for members yet. The biggest problems are in the flow itself, not in how it looks: a member can believe they've reserved a tool when they haven't, can reserve the same thing twice, or can confirm a pick-up day the library can't honour. Dark mode and phone layout have smaller problems, and those are quick to fix.

I checked phone and desktop widths in light and dark mode, plus a keyboard-only pass. Independent reviewers found the problems, and each one was reproduced in the running site before it counted. None of this comes from testing with real members, so treat the "may confuse members" items as predictions.

## Fix first

1. **"Reserve this tool" only adds the tool to a basket.** The "Added to your basket" message disappears after a few seconds and has no link to the basket. A first-time member may close the page thinking the drill is reserved. Make the message stay, add a "Go to basket" button, and use wording that shows the reservation isn't finished (`app.js:271`).
2. **When the basket hold runs out, the member is stuck.** After about 10 minutes, Continue only shows "Something went wrong. Try again." Every retry fails, and reloading doesn't help. That will hit people who reserve in the evening while doing something else. Tell them how long tools are held, and when time runs out, explain what happened and let them start again (`app.js:94`).
3. **Tapping Confirm twice makes two reservations.** We got FT-4471 and FT-4472 this way. There's no sign that anything is happening for about 1.5 seconds after the tap, so a second tap is likely. Disable the button and show progress while it's working (`app.js:413`).
4. **The pick-up day can be wrong.**
   - The calendar accepts closed days and days before a tool is back. A pressure washer booked for 10 October, a week before it's available, went all the way to "Reservation confirmed". A closed Monday is only rejected after Confirm, and the error has no link back to change the day.
   - The basket then asks for the session again without using the day already chosen.
   - The sessions are shown latest first, while keyboard and screen readers go through them earliest first (`styles.css:818–819`).
   - Only let members pick open days when the tool is available, and pre-select that session in the basket (`app.js:198`, `app.js:265`).
5. **Keyboard users get stuck in the loan-length list.** Once it's open, Tab only moves between "One week" and "Two weeks", so you can't leave without choosing. Esc doesn't close it either (`app.js:238–251`). This is a WCAG failure and a small fix.

## Dark mode

- The green "Available from …" labels on the tool list fail the WCAG contrast minimum in dark mode: 3.07:1 against the 4.5:1 required. The dark-mode green (`--color-ok`, `styles.css:60`) has drifted from the value in your design notes, and those labels also lose their background in dark mode. It's a one-line token fix.
- Everything else I looked at in dark mode reads well, including the error messages and the confirm page.

## Phones

- **Search is below all ten tools on a phone.** The search box and filters come after the tenth card (`index.html:36`).
- **Tool names are cut to one line.** Both drills read "Cordless drill 18 V, co…", so members can't tell the two-battery drill from the other one (`styles.css:377`). The same rule cuts names off at 200% text size, which matters for members who use larger text.
- **The tool list is too wide for the smallest phones.** At 320 px it scrolls sideways, because of a 330 px minimum column width (`styles.css:331`).
- **The fixed "Reserve this tool" bar covers content.** It hides calendar days and "One week" from keyboard focus, and the "Two weeks" option opens underneath it. The bar needs space reserved below the page content (`styles.css:758`).

## Also worth fixing

- A search with no matches still shows the whole list instead of saying nothing was found.
- "Basket (1)" still shows after the reservation is confirmed.
- Membership numbers without "FT-" and mobile numbers written as "+44…" are rejected, and the error reads as if the field were empty.
- The done page shows reservation number FT-4471 even when no reservation was made.

## Keep these

- The confirm page's error messages are well done: one summary links to each field, the examples are clear, and what members typed is kept.
- The confirm page says plainly that nothing is paid online.
- The done page tells members where to go, what to bring and what to do if they miss the session.
- The calendar reads out full dates and which days the library is open.

## Where it stands

- The flow doesn't pass the basic machine checks yet, and you're aiming for human-confirmed. What blocks it is the keyboard, reflow, contrast and text-size failures above.
- The three design reviewers also found the look plain and generic: the same wrench placeholder on every tool, and nothing that's distinctly Fernhill's. That matters less than the flow problems.
- Real screen-reader checks (VoiceOver and TalkBack) and testing with real members haven't been done.

I couldn't ask you, so I took the audience, devices and accessibility needs from `PRODUCT.md`. I assumed that only the reservation flow was in scope.

If you'd like, I can fix items 1–5 and the dark-mode contrast one at a time, re-checking each fix. Before launch, it's also worth watching three or four members try a reservation on their own phones. That would show whether point 1 really trips people up.
